html:
The Yugambeh are an Aboriginal Australian people of the country from the Logan River south to the Tweed, which today includes the Gold Coast of Queensland and its hinterland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land runs from beaches and estuaries up to the rainforest of the McPherson Range. Seafood, fish runs and forest foods made it a rich place to live. Their language, Yugambeh, is closely related to Bundjalung, their neighbours to the south. Timber cutters came for the red cedar in the 1840s, then sugar and cattle. The Gold Coast grew as a resort in the 20th century on Yugambeh land. Another neighbour on the map is the Ngarabal. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
